Heat loss is the steady loss with the kiln held at top temperature. It does not include the heat stored in the walls and ware during the firing.

Cylinders joined in parallel are assumed to add their capacities. That is a reasonable inference at the same temperature and fill, but no source states it. Never warm a cylinder with a flame or heater.
Gas piping, regulators, safety valves and the installation must be done or checked by a licensed gas fitter to your local code (NFPA 54 and 58 in the US).
The front wall is the door: bricked up, dry, for each firing. Lay the inner and outer courses together, staggered, with a header course two-thirds of the way up.
Side-mounted burners need a bag wall so the flames don't hit the ware: hard brick, first course solid in front of the burners.
Damper: a kiln shelf in a slot 12 in wide and one course high, about a foot above the top of the flue. Brace the chimney with angle at its corners and tie it to the kiln frame.
4 spy holes, 2 in round, up the door, a few inches off centre so they miss the shelf posts. Cone packs in the top and bottom, draw rings in the middle.
